motion.summary: The declaration I will fear no evil. first assembles on a straight reading line in the dark wall above two seated people. Once complete, its individual letters spread and rotate along an arch; small footing marks appear at the ends. The people and their comforting gesture remain beneath the whole sentence.
phases: 135.2–137.1s: complete the declaration as a conventional readable line above the seated pair.
138.8–139.7s: bend the intact phrase into an arch using per-letter positions and rotations.
139.7–141.7s: hold the completed arch above the people with two restrained footing marks.
motion.transferablePrinciple: Read the complete promise first, then let the entire sentence become a protective spatial relationship around its human subject while keeping the same words and reading order.
variations: After a different reassurance is read, let its words form a low bridge across a gap between two people.
Turn a completed homecoming phrase into two sheltering sides around a newly composed doorway, without copying this arch or image.
cautions: Use only when the scene has enough clear space and a real semantic reason for the shape; curved lettering is not a default decorative treatment.
Keep letter rotation moderate and spacing open; the sloped terminal words are harder to read than the original straight line.
Preserve a complete reading hold before spatial deformation and generate new artwork for the new story.
